title: Merchandise Purchases Policy Manual — One Purchase Record per Unit
content:
**Clause.** Under Merchandise Purchases a customer may hold any number of purchase records; there is no maximum per customer. Every unit bought is its own purchase record, and the units of one order or register transaction share that transaction's order number. Each record keeps its own merchandise class, return window, price adjustments and refund. A return, a cancellation or a price adjustment always names the single purchase record it concerns, and never applies to an order number as a whole.

## The clause restated

| Question the clause answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| How many purchase records may one customer hold? | Any number; no maximum is set. |
| What is one purchase record? | One unit of one item bought in one order or register transaction. |
| What do the units of one transaction have in common? | The order number of the transaction. |
| Which terms belong to the record rather than to the order? | Its merchandise class, its return window, its price adjustments and its refund. |
| What does a return, cancellation or adjustment act on? | One named purchase record, never an order number as a whole. |

## Hypothetical illustration

An online order (hypothetical) contains two identical sweaters and one table lamp. It produces three purchase records under one order number: two Apparel, Shoes & Accessories records and one Home & Kitchen record. Each sweater has its own return window and its own price-adjustment history, and returning one sweater names that sweater's purchase record only; the other sweater and the lamp are untouched.
